JERUSALEM: Israel 's parliament was sworn in on Tuesday (Nov 10) without a new government , after a deadlocked general election stripped Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power.
Lawmakers elected in the Oct 27 vote took their oaths of office as Gadi Eisenkot , a former general, sought to forge a coalition after Israel 's president tasked him on Sunday with forming a government .
Eisenkot and his allies also lack a majority and he has yet to strike deals with parties that could bring him to power. If both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form coalitions, another election could follow.
Presiding over the swearing-in ceremony, President Isaac Herzog told lawmakers: "You must do everything to avoid a repeat election."

"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals ... Look upon one another with generosity. There is much work to be done here, and it requires the ability and experience found in every part of this House."

PARLIAMENT COULD TRY TO SET UP OCT 7 INQUIRY Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new candidate manages to form a coalition. His right-wing Likud party's alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority, now holding 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats.
Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar party and patchwork partner factions hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in Israel 's Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu .
This means that the newly sworn-in parliament could still deliver on some of Eisenkot's campaign promises, such as potentially setting up a commission of inquiry into the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attacks, something backed by the Arab parties but largely opposed by Netanyahu .
It also could allow Eisenkot to replace the current Knesset speaker, a Likud member.
Herzog told Knesset members that parliament was "duty bound to leave no stone unturned" in investigating and understanding the "catastrophe" of Oct 7, while Israel continues to face threats from Iran and its proxies.
Eisenkot initially has until Dec 6 to form a government but he can seek a two-week extension to Dec 20. He has acknowledged his path to power is "extraordinarily complex".
His options include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support, bringing ultra-Orthodox parties into his camp despite years of mutual hostility, or forging a unity government with Netanyahu . All three paths face formidable obstacles.
Ultra-Orthodox parties have so far said they would not join an Eisenkot-led government .

Related:

How Israel's new parliament can make Netanyahu's life difficult

Netanyahu rival Eisenkot seeks 'wide' government but path to power uncertain

Israel faces new era of sinking US support after election

For his part, Netanyahu has cast doubt on the election results by baselessly alleging voter fraud by Arabs, who make up a fifth of the population. Election officials have said they are probing potential misconduct, but that they have seen no evidence of fraud that could have influenced the vote's outcome.
Speaking after parliament was sworn in, Netanyahu called for a unity government , warning that Iran was seeking to revive its nuclear programme and that Israel could come under growing international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran.
"Only such a (unity) government will be capable of confronting challenges of this magnitude," he said.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government , Herzog would likely ask Netanyahu to try to build a coalition. If he also fails, another candidate would get a chance before Israel would be forced into another election.
Moments after the official opening of parliament, Eisenkot and his allies submitted a series of bills, including legislation to establish a state commission of inquiry into the Oct 7 attacks and to impose term limits on the prime minister. They also proposed repealing a controversial judicial overhaul and other laws enacted under Netanyahu 's government over the past four years.
Among those sworn in on Tuesday was Elisha Madan, a military reservist who lost both legs fighting in Gaza. He received a standing ovation from lawmakers as he rose on his prosthetic legs to take the oath of office.

Source: Reuters/fs

Nvidia selloff deepens, adding to AI jitters

The Nvidia logo outside Nvidia's Shanghai office building in Shanghai, China, November 10, 2026. REUTERS/Go Nakamura

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 10 : Technology shares were in the red again on Tuesday, with Anthropic's steps toward a big IPO failing to calm general anxiety about the health of the AI sector.
Selling was driven by a hot US inflation report that increased expectations the Federal Reserve will raise rates again next month, alongside Nvidia's hiring lawyers for an internal investigation tied to its CEO and the development of an Ohio data center getting more complicated. 
Many investors remained optimistic about the prospects for AI investments while allowing that volatility has become a fact of market life this fall. The Nasdaq Composite was off 1 per cent on Tuesday afternoon. Over the past month, the index has dropped by 1 per cent or more eight times and risen by 1 per cent or more six times. 
"There is concern about what happens at the top at Nvidia, and if he's replaced, who's he replaced with," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York, who said he sees selling in Nvidia and other major AI firms as buying opportunities. "But I don’t see Nvidia falling apart. I see a very strong company hit by something not of its own making."

Besides Nvidia, down 6.5 per cent, the major decliners were mostly big beneficiaries of the AI rally that swept markets for the first two-thirds of this year. Server maker Dell Technologies was down 4.8 per cent on Tuesday but up 161 per cent for the year, according to LSEG data, while chip firm Sandisk was down 4.5 per cent for the day and up 257 per cent for the year.
Among the neoclouds, smaller AI infrastructure firms that have been under pressure this month amid concerns about their capacity to raise funds under tighter market conditions, Iren dropped 10 per cent, Nebius fell 7 per cent and CoreWeave slid 3 per cent. All three have declined by at least 40 per cent since the Nasdaq hit its most recent high on October 6. CoreWeave is due to report earnings after the close on Tuesday.
Many investors said they thought general market anxiety was behind much of the selling, despite a newsy day across AI-related subjects. British cloud services provider Nscale is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, The Telegraph reported on Tuesday.
Shares of power equipment maker GE Vernova slid more than 6 per cent on Tuesday, after Japanese investment firm SoftBank revised equipment procurement plans for its US data center projects. GE Vernova is among the companies involved in the development of SoftBank's colossal gas-fired power plant and data center in Pike County, Ohio, analysts said.
Nvidia’s was on track to shed more than $470 billion in market value over two sessions as concerns mounted over the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. 
Even so, investors were mostly focused on the longer-term picture. 
"We can always ascribe a reason as to why things are more volatile. And they have been more volatile the last few weeks for sure, since October, let's call it," said Jason Ware, chief investment officer at Albion Financial Group in Salt Lake City, Utah. "But at the end of the day, the path for stocks over the coming weeks and months is going to be really a story of earnings."
Following Tuesday’s inflation report, many investors will be focusing on the next big events for technology stocks, which stand to be Nvidia’s earnings report after the close a week from today and Anthropic’s IPO in the days after, regardless of what stocks do on a given day. 
“We're probably gonna have record earnings again next year unless we see a recession or a massive pivoting on AI capex, and I don't expect either one,” said Ware, whose firm owns Nvidia. “And so I think that's going to be the signal is the trajectory of earnings, the economy growing more than 2 per cent. And the rest of this is sort of just short-term noise that will, like I said, get ironed out over time." 

Source: Reuters

items.title: 英警察、米陸軍兵士を逮捕　ロシア情報機関への協力容疑
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ロンドン １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ロンドン １０日 ロイター] - 英警察は１０日、ロシアの情報機関に協力した疑いで米陸軍の上級兵士の男（４１）をイングランド西部グロスター近郊で逮捕したと発表した。

米連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）のカシュ・パテル長官は、兵士の逮捕について「米国と同盟国にとって極めて重大な懸念であるスパイ行為の疑惑」に関連すると述べた。

米陸軍防諜司令部のショーン・スティンチョン司令官（准将）は「機密情報を託された上級兵士の今回の疑惑は、内部からの脅威が現実に存在し、絶えず続いていることを厳粛に受け止めるべき形で示している」と語った。

英警察は、この逮捕は「対テロ警察が現在進めている他のいかなる捜査とも関連していない」と説明した。

米軍は９日、英国の空軍基地から航空機を退避させた。こうした動きは３カ月間で２回目となる。

items.title: US Household Delinquencies Rise Slightly, NY Fed Report Shows
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: US consumers are falling further behind on their debts as they navigate higher costs on fuel, groceries and other goods.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- US consumers are falling further behind on their debts as they navigate higher costs on fuel, groceries and other goods. The share of overdue consumer loans rose marginally in the third quarter to 5% from 4.7% the prior quarter, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit released Tuesday. Total household debt balances rose 1.8% to $19.1 trillion. The share of mortgage balances more than 90 days overdue rose to 1.13%, the highest since the first quarter of 2018. The portion of mortgage debt transitioning into early and severe delinquency ticked up but remained near pre-pandemic norms, New York Fed researchers said. “Although delinquency transition rates for housing debts have crept up, the overall credit quality of these loans remains strong,” Donghoon Lee, economic research adviser at the New York Fed, said in a press release. Balances for home equity lines of credit rose by $23 billion, marking the largest increase since 2005 and the 18th straight quarter of growth. The share of debt becoming newly delinquent also rose for auto loans. Student loan balances increased slightly but loans entered delinquency at a slower pace.Transition into delinquency also improved for credit cards. In a blog post accompanying the data, New York Fed researchers found delinquency rates for cards opened during the pandemic — when issuance rose for consumers with lower incomes and credit scores — are declining. “If current patterns hold, the elevated delinquencies of the past few years may prove to be more of a pandemic-era echo than a permanent feature of the credit card market,” they wrote. Pandemic DelinquenciesSeparate data released Tuesday by the Urban Institute, a think tank in Washington, D.C., suggest people have fallen further behind on debts since the pandemic. About 5.8% of Americans have at least some delinquent credit card debt, with a median amount of $680 debt being late. That’s up from 4.3% who had some credit card delinquency in August 2019, according to the institute’s research. Around 5.5% of consumers have some delinquency in auto and retail loans, compared with 3.9% in August 2019.Nationwide, about 24% of US consumers with a credit file have debt of any kind in collections, according to the institute. That’s down from the roughly 30% who had debt in collections just before the pandemic, though part of the improvement likely stems from delays in reporting collections to credit bureaus, said Breno Braga, a senior fellow at the institute. Residents of ZIP codes with a majority of people of color are 50% more likely to have debt in collections than residents of majority white areas, the study found.The institute tracked the share of people across the US with debt in collections or delinquent by taking a representative sample of credit bureau records from August 2026.Consumer price data released Tuesday showed underlying inflation excluding food and energy rose 0.3% in October from a month earlier, topping estimates for the third straight month.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.summary: ＜ロンドン株式市場＞　まちまちで取引を終えた。金価格の反落を受け、貴金属株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反落した。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１６％続伸した。    ＦＴＳＥ３５０種貴金属株指数は４．７２％安。貴金属採掘フレスニヨは４．７％、エンデバー・マイニングは４．３％、銅大手アントファガスタは２．１％いずれも下落した。    石油・ガス株指数は１．６７％安。トランプ米大統領がイランへの軍事攻撃を当面見送る姿勢を示したことを受け、北海ブレント原油先物価格は節目の１バレル＝９０ドルを一時割り込んだ。    一方、飲料株指数は０．８７％、生活必需品株指数は０．７４％それぞれ上昇。小売り大手マークス・アンド・スペンサー（Ｍ＆Ｓ）は４．１％高だった。
items.body:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞　まちまちで取引を終えた。金価格の反落を受け、貴金属株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反落した。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１６％続伸した。    ＦＴＳＥ３５０種貴金属株指数は４．７２％安。貴金属採掘フレスニヨは４．７％、エンデバー・マイニングは４．３％、銅大手アントファガスタは２．１％いずれも下落した。    石油・ガス株指数は１．６７％安。トランプ米大統領がイランへの軍事攻撃を当面見送る姿勢を示したことを受け、北海ブレント原油先物価格は節目の１バレル＝９０ドルを一時割り込んだ。    一方、飲料株指数は０．８７％、生活必需品株指数は０．７４％それぞれ上昇。小売り大手マークス・アンド・スペンサー（Ｍ＆Ｓ）は４．１％高だった。    イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のロンバルデリ副総裁は、１２月会合での利上げの可能性を排除しないとの見解を示した。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場では１２月に２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げが決まる可能性を約５０％と見込んでいる。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　続伸して取引を終えた。米イラン間の軍事衝突への懸念が後退し、原油先物価格が下落したことが投資家心理を後押しした。米国株と比べて欧州株に相対的な割安感が出ていることも、投資家が資金を振り向けやすい環境になっているとの指摘もある。    ＳＴＯＸＸユーロ圏銀行株指数は１．６８％上昇した。銀行株の比重が大きいスペインのＩＢＥＸ指数は０．９８％高だった。    米当局がイランに対する大規模な軍事作戦の必要性に否定的な見方を示したことを受け、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種石油・ガス株指数は１．６０％下落した。    フランスの決済プラットフォーム、エデンレッドは６．４％上昇。ブラジルでの司法判断を受け、買われた。    ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、欧州の主要企業の２０２６年第３・四半期（２６年７－９月期）の利益は約２５％増と、従来予想約１６％増を上回る見込みだ。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　国債利回りが上昇した。米インフレ指標が予想を上回ったことで米国債利回りが上昇したことに追随した。    ドイツの２年債利回りは６ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇して３．０７％となり、１日の上昇幅としては１カ月ぶりの大きさとなる見通し。ユーロ圏の指標となる１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ上昇して３．３０％となった。    いずれも欧州時間の午前中の取引では低下していたが、１０月の米消費者物価（ＣＰＩ）が前月比０．４％上昇と予想を上回る伸びを示し、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が来月利上げする軌道にあることが示されたことを受け、上昇に転じた。nL6N46R141    これを受けて米２年債利回りは１６ｂｐ上昇、指標の１０年債利回りは１２ｂｐ上昇して４．９９％となった。    リーガン・キャピタルの最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、スカイラー・ウェイナンド氏は、今回のデータについて「ＦＲＢが明らかなインフレ加速を無視できないことは明白であり、１２月の追加利上げの下地が整った」と述べた。    米インフレ指標の上振れが欧州経済に直接波及するわけではないが、米国債の動きが他の市場に波及することは多い。    その他のユーロ圏国債利回りも、米インフレ指標を受けて上昇した。    フランスの１０年債利回りは４ｂｐ上昇して４．７８％となった。序盤には、エネルギー価格の下落を受けて一時約６ｂｐ低下する場面もあった。    イタリアの１０年債利回りも同程度上昇し、４．３５％となった。

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　国債利回りが上昇した。米インフレ指標が予想を上回ったことで米国債利回りが上昇したことに追随した。    ドイツの２年債利回りは６ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇して３．０７％となり、１日の上昇幅としては１カ月ぶりの大きさとなる見通し。ユーロ圏の指標となる１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ上昇して３．３０％となった。    いずれも欧州時間の午前中の取引では低下していたが、１０月の米消費者物価（ＣＰＩ）が前月比０．４％上昇と予想を上回る伸びを示し、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が来月利上げする軌道にあることが示されたことを受け、上昇に転じた。nL6N46R141    これを受けて米２年債利回りは１６ｂｐ上昇、指標の１０年債利回りは１２ｂｐ上昇して４．９９％となった。    リーガン・キャピタルの最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、スカイラー・ウェイナンド氏は、今回のデータについて「ＦＲＢが明らかなインフレ加速を無視できないことは明白であり、１２月の追加利上げの下地が整った」と述べた。    米インフレ指標の上振れが欧州経済に直接波及するわけではないが、米国債の動きが他の市場に波及することは多い。    その他のユーロ圏国債利回りも、米インフレ指標を受けて上昇した。    フランスの１０年債利回りは４ｂｐ上昇して４．７８％となった。序盤には、エネルギー価格の下落を受けて一時約６ｂｐ低下する場面もあった。    イタリアの１０年債利回りも同程度上昇し、４．３５％となった。

Nov 10 : Nscale, a British cloud provider backed by chip giant Nvidia, is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, the Telegraph reported on Tuesday.
Executives at the data-centre developer are assessing whether to pause efforts to go public until next year, the report added.
Nscale did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours.
The report comes days after Reuters reported that Microsoft had declined an option to expand its existing agreement with Nscale to rent more computing power at a Texas data center.

items.title: Further interest rate hikes might be needed: Bank of Canada
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: The Bank of Canada’s governing council thinks it might need to raise interest rates further, but it’s proceeding carefully, according to a summary of deliberations.
items.body: OTTAWA — The Bank of Canada’s governing council thinks it might need to raise interest rates further, but it’s proceeding carefully, according to a summary of deliberations of its recent decision to raise its key policy rate for the first time since 2023. According to the report, the council acknowledged it faced considerable uncertainty and said it would take its monetary policy decisions one meeting at a time. The Bank of Canada raised its policy interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 2.5 per cent last month to reduce the risk that stubbornly high oil prices become persistent inflation. The summary says the council members agreed that monetary policy cannot lower global energy prices, but can prevent them from leading to generalized inflation. The decision came as the Bank of Canada raised its outlook for the annual inflation rate to hit 3.5 per cent at the end of this year and remain above three per cent for much of 2027. The summary of deliberations said higher costs largely haven’t been passed through to consumers so far, but the bank’s surveys suggest businesses expect to raise some prices over the next year. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 10, 2026.

items.title: US Bitcoin ETFs Lose $201M as BlackRock Withdrawals Extend the Slump
items.summary: US-listed spot Bitcoin funds recorded another difficult session on Monday, November 9. The updated Farside Investors flow table shows $201.0 million in net outflows across the group, extending a three ...
items.body:
News
/ NewsBTC
/ US Bitcoin ETFs Lose $201M as BlackRock Withdrawals Extend the Slump

US Bitcoin ETFs Lose $201M as BlackRock Withdrawals Extend the Slump 2 min read

BLK BTCUSD
US-listed spot Bitcoin funds recorded another difficult session on Monday, November 9. The updated Farside Investors flow table shows $201.0 million in net outflows across the group, extending a three-session losing streak. The important detail is that the negative total was not evenly spread across issuers: BlackRock’s IBIT recorded $213.2 million leaving, while Morgan Stanley’s MSBT attracted $22.1 million.
TL;DR: Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost a net $201.0 million on November 9, following $430.2 million on November 5 and $411.9 million on November 6. BlackRock drove Monday’s withdrawals, while one smaller fund reported inflows. The figures measure fund creations and redemptions, not the intentions of every Bitcoin investor.
Three sessions that add up to more than $1 billion
The latest fully reported Farside figures put the consecutive negative sessions at roughly $1.04 billion in aggregate . Thursday’s $430.2 million loss was followed by Friday’s $411.9 million and then Monday’s $201.0 million. That progression shows persistent selling pressure, although Monday’s net outflow was smaller than either of the previous two sessions.
Our previous report on Friday’s fund activity documented a similar pattern of issuer concentration. Going back further, the November 2 breakdown shows why it is worth examining individual ETF lines rather than reading the aggregate as a single institutional vote.
On November 9, ARK Invest and 21Shares’ ARKB showed a $9.9 million outflow. The positive contribution from MSBT offset part of the selling elsewhere. Several other funds showed no daily net creation or redemption. That does not mean no shares changed hands on exchanges; secondary-market trading and flows into or out of a fund’s underlying Bitcoin exposure are different measures.
Why IBIT carries so much of the story
BlackRock’s fund is a large and closely watched route into Bitcoin for investors using traditional brokerage and portfolio systems. Its persistent redemptions can therefore affect the tone of market commentary disproportionately. But the identity of an ETF’s end investors is not published in a daily flow table, and a withdrawal cannot automatically be attributed to hedge funds, pensions or retail holders.
The distinction between net flows and assets under management matters as well. A fund’s reported assets can fall when Bitcoin’s price drops even without corresponding redemptions. Conversely, share creations can occur on a day when the asset price weakens. Analysts who blend these concepts can make demand appear stronger or weaker than it actually was.
What would signal a more durable turn?
The next test is whether the large-issuer selling eases over several completed reporting sessions. One positive day would interrupt the streak but would not, by itself, demonstrate that buyers have regained control. It is also worth watching whether inflows broaden across products or remain confined to a single issuer.
These numbers are current through the November 9 US trading session , not an estimate of November 10 while trading is still under way. A better measure of sentiment combines a completed ETF flow series with spot volume, derivatives positioning and the changing rates outlook. For now, the latest evidence is that listed-fund demand remains weak even as the scale of net redemptions has moderated from last week’s peaks.
Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

items.title: 再送-ロシア、ウクライナ10州の送電網攻撃　冬控えエネルギー施設標的
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
(第１段落の州の表記を修正して再送しました)

[１０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
(第１段落の州の表記を修正して再送しました)

[１０日 ロイター] -  ウクライナのポルタワ、ドニプロペトロウスクなど１０州がロシア軍による攻撃を受け、広範囲にわたり停電が発生した。ウクライナ当局者らが１０日、明らかにした。主要変電所５カ所が標的となり、２人が死亡したという。冬を控える中、ロシアによるエネルギー施設を狙った空爆作戦の一環とみられる。

ロシアとウクライナは今年２月以来となる米仲介による協議を１０－１１日にアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）の首都アブダビで開催している。

ウクライナのコレツキー首相は通信アプリ「テレグラム」で、ビンニツァ、キロボフラードも含めた各州の変電所がロシア軍による攻撃を受けたと投稿。これに先立ち、ウクライナ国営電力会社ウクレネルゴは、ロシアが夜から朝にかけてウクライナ８州のエネルギーインフラを攻撃し、キーウ、ハルキウ、ドニプロペトロウスクなど６州の家庭で停電が発生したと発表した。

ロシアはここ数カ月、物流施設を含む経済への打撃を狙った空爆を強めている。キロボフラード州の知事によると、大手ホームセンターなどの民間インフラも攻撃を受けた。ドニプロペトロウスク州当局によると、ドローン（無人機）による攻撃があったという。

ウクライナは、弾道ミサイルやジェット推進型無人機を迎撃する兵器不足に直面しており、ロシアの攻撃阻止が課題となっている。

Plug Power, JELD-WEN, Trex, GE Vernova, and Hertz shares are falling, what you need to know 2 min read

PLUG JELD TREX GEV

What happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index increased 0.4 percent in October 2026, highlighting persistent price pressures across the economy.
The latest inflation figures showed that underlying inflation remains resilient, with the core Consumer Price Index—which excludes volatile food and energy costs—advancing 0.3 percent over the month. Sticky inflation complicates corporate operating environments by elevating input costs and weakening consumer spending power.
When consumer price gauges climb faster than expected, market participants often reassess future earnings expectations, particularly for high-growth technology firms whose future cash flows are heavily sensitive to macroeconomic headwinds. Sector-wide sentiment turned cautious as investors factored in the potential durability of elevated cost structures across operations.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Renewable energy company Plug Power PLUG fell 8.7%. Is now the time to buy Plug Power? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free.
Home construction materials company JELD-WEN JELD fell 12.8%. Is now the time to buy JELD-WEN? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free.
Home construction materials company Trex TREX fell 7.1%. Is now the time to buy Trex? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free.
Electrical systems company GE Vernova GEV fell 7.2%. Is now the time to buy GE Vernova? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free.
Ground transportation company Hertz HTZ fell 4.6%. Is now the time to buy Hertz? Access our full analysis report here, it’s free.
Zooming in on JELD-WEN (JELD)
JELD-WEN’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 98 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for JELD-WEN and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was about 24 hours ago when the stock gained 12.1% on the news that falling crude oil prices fueled a broad market rebound and eased cost concerns surrounding artificial intelligence data center construction. CNBC reported that the major indexes rallied as oil prices dropped. In the session, Brent was down about 4% to around $94 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate was down about 3% to around $87. United States equities rallied to claw back losses from the prior week as retreating crude benchmarks alleviated inflationary headwinds across major industries.
Lower energy prices are particularly advantageous for energy-intensive sectors, offering timely relief to developers scaling artificial intelligence facilities. Construction of hyperscale data centers requires substantial capital and power resources, making sustained high energy costs a threat to projected operating margins. As fuel costs swung lower, concerns regarding buildout budgets diminished, driving broad-based investor optimism across the technology and infrastructure ecosystem.
JELD-WEN is down 58.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $1.04 per share, it is trading 67.5% below its 52-week high of $3.18 from January 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of JELD-WEN’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $39.22.

items.author: Mining.com

items.summary: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a
items.body: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a bigger interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year. Spot gold XAU= was down 2.8% at $4,021.36 per ounce by 11:33 a.m. ET (1635 GMT). US gold futures GCcv1 for December delivery fell 1.9% to $4,036.00 per ounce. “I think it’s a bit of a short-term negative for gold because the inflation numbers were running a little higher than expected,” said Edward Meir, an analyst at Marex. The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month after advancing 0.6% in September, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.3% month-on-month rise. Bets on a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike in December started to build after the inflation print and comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support more aggressive action in the event of a too-hot Consumer Price Index report. The probability of a 25 bp hike is fully priced in, while the possibility of a 50 bp hike rose to 10.5% from 0% before the data, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. The US dollar .DXY rose against a basket of other major currencies, and Treasury yields climbed. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for overseas buyers, while higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. “(Gold) continues to trade above the critical $4,000/oz mark,” Standard Chartered said in a note, adding “crude oil, inflation risks and equity markets continue to set the tone of trading for gold with a focus on rate hike expectations for the December Fed meeting.” Meanwhile, the Monetary Authority of Singapore said it would launch a vaulting service to hold bullion for foreign central banks and lower taxes on some companies in the gold market as it competes for a bigger slice of the precious metals trade. Spot silver XAG= fell 3.9% to $51.32 per ounce and palladium XPD= was down 2.0% at $1,021.22. (Reporting by Vedika Thorat and Anjana Anil in Bengaluru; Editing by Kirsten Donovan and Jonathan Ananda)

US skips UN human rights review, drawing criticism

The meeting was postponed until January after Washington refused to take part, saying participation would imply support for the UN Human Rights Council.

The empty seat of the US delegation, during the 60th session of the Human Rights Council, at the European headquarters of the United Nations in Geneva, Switzerland, on Sep 8, 2025. (Photo: AP/Salvatore Di Nolfi)

GENEVA: The Un ited States spurned a UN meeting on Tuesday (Nov 10) where its human rights record un der US President Donald Trump was due to be examined, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations have surged to levels not seen in decades.
Washington disengaged from the Geneva-based UN Human Rights Co un cil last year, citing an anti-Israel bias, and this is the second year in a row that it has skipped its own review - a process that even authoritarian state s take part in.
The US left its seat on the stage of the UN meeting empty and the council decided to postpone the event until January.
A US State Department spokesperson said participation would imply endorsement of the co un cil's work.

"This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own 'values' as it p us hes anti-American rhetoric," the spokesperson said, without responding to allegations about the US record.
The 47-member co un cil has not directly criticised Washington's rights record but its appointed experts have, such as over migrant deportations. Washington said deportations wer e carried out in accordance with US immigration law.

QUESTIONS ON ABORTION AND DEATH PENALTY The Un iversal Periodic Review asks all 193 UN member states to submit a rights report every few years and these are review ed by other states , which provide non-binding recommendations.
UN documents show co un tries had planned on Tuesday to raise issues such as abortion and the death penalty.
US and international non-governmental organisations also sent nearly 200 UN submissions covering topics from migration to racial discrimination.
“We've seen attacks on f un damental human rights and civil liberties un precedented in generations," Jamil Dakwar , of the American Civil Liberties Un ion , told reporters in Geneva. "Enough is enough."
Fourteen co un tries are due to take part in the review process in Geneva this month. In Trump's first term in office, the US submitted its UPR report.
Noor Abdalla, wife of pro-Palestinian student activist Mahmoud Khalil, who was held in immigration detention last year, is among campaigners pressing UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk to promptly hold a briefing on the US rights situation, even in Washington's absence.
"When the most powerful government in the world is not held acco un table, they think that they can do whatever they want," Abdalla told reporters.
However, diplomats were sceptical given that few states want to confront Washington.
"The view is to leave the door open and hope they come back in two years," said a diplomat.

items.title: ドイツ銀、ＦＲＢの27年1月追加利上げを予想
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[１０日 ロイター] - ドイツ銀行は１０日、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が２０２７年１月に２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の追加利上げを実施するとの見通しを示した。１０月のインフレ指標が予想を上回り、利上げ観測が強まったことを受けた。

ドイツ銀は「今日発表された消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は引き続き幅広い項目で上昇を示し、物価上昇圧力の根強さについてこれまで抱いていた懸念を強める内容となった」と指摘した。

従来はＦＲＢが１２月と２７年３月に利上げすると予想していた。

労働省発表の１０月のＣＰＩは前月比０．４％上昇。伸びはロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想の０．３％を上回った。９月は０．６％上昇していた。変動の大きい食品とエネルギーを除くコアＣＰＩは前月比０．３％上昇。エコノミスト予想は０．２％上昇だった。nL6N46R141

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場が織り込む１２月の利上げ確率はほぼ９９％となっている。

こうした中、ＦＲＢのウォラー理事は１０日、米国の１０月のインフレ率が鈍化したとしてもＦＲＢは１２月の会合で利上げを支持する考えを示し、物価情勢が悪化した場合は０．５％ポイントの大幅利上げを検討する必要があると述べた。 nL6N46R11A

これに対しドイツ銀は「ウォラー理事の発言は、１２月に５０ｂｐ利上げする可能性を示した。われわれもその可能性は排除しないが、利上げ幅の拡大は基本シナリオではない」と述べた。

items.title: US CPI Exceeds Expectations Again, Waller's Warning Comes True! Wall Street Focuses on Whether December Rate Hike Will Be 25 or 50 Basis Points; "New Fed News Agency": Stop-and-Go Strategy Faces Test
items.author: 华尔街见闻
items.creator: 华尔街见闻
items.summary: The "New Federal Reserve Newsletter" pointed out that before the release of the CPI, Waller suggested the possibility of a 50-basis-point rate hike in December, and so far, no other Fed officials have publicly responded. In addition to a single 50-basis-point hike, the Fed may also choose to signal consecutive rate hikes in December and January. Wall Street generally believes that inflationary pressures remain stubborn, further strengthening the case for a rate hike in December, though a 50-basis-point increase is not a consensus. The market is concerned about whether the Fed will extend the tightening cycle.
items.body: US inflation in October once again exceeded expectations, further raising market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with the possibility of a larger rate increase now being discussed. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced on Tuesday, November 10, that the October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month, lower than the 0.6% increase in September but higher than economists’ forecasts of 0.3%. The core CPI rose 0.3% month-on-month, matching September’s increase and exceeding the market’s expectation of 0.2%. This marks the third consecutive month where overall CPI rose more than Wall Street predicted, and core CPI has also climbed 0.3% month-on-month for three straight months. Due to the failure to collect CPI data during the US federal government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS was unable to provide a year-on-year figure for October CPI. This report precisely meets the policy threshold previously outlined by Federal Reserve Governor Waller. Just hours before the CPI was published, Waller stated that if the core CPI for October increased by 0.3% or more month-on-month, he might support a 50 basis point rate hike at the Fed’s monetary policy meeting in December. With this criterion now met, the market’s bets on a 50 basis point rate hike in December have gained momentum. Nick Timiraos, a journalist nicknamed the “New Fed Whisperer,” pointed out that this inflation report is testing the Fed’s previous strategy of “spacing out rate hikes,” using staggered moves to leave room to monitor economic data. The choices facing policymakers are not only between a 25 or 50 basis point hike in December, but also whether to adjust the pace of subsequent actions, or even to signal back-to-back rate hikes in December and January of next year. Wall Street’s reaction is showing a common assessment: inflationary pressures remain stubborn, providing more justification for a December rate hike, though opinions differ on the size of the increase. Some believe that three consecutive months of core CPI climbing 0.3% makes it difficult for the Fed to ignore the inflation rebound; others feel that a 50-basis-point hike may be too aggressive and that 25 basis points is still the more realistic option. The market’s real concern is not just the decision at the next meeting but also whether the Fed may extend the tightening cycle as a result. “New Fed Whisperer”: Core prices strengthen across the board, Fed could signal back-to-back hikes In his analysis in The Wall Street Journal, Timiraos noted that the strong showing of October inflation is testing the Fed’s strategy of spreading out rate hikes across different meetings to allow time to observe economic data. He noted that Waller has raised the possibility that if the third month’s inflation data remains hot, a 50-basis-point rate hike in December could be on the table. However, no other Fed officials have publicly echoed this position as of yet. The Fed could also choose another way to address inflationary pressures: instead of a one-off 50-basis-point increase at a single meeting, it could signal consecutive rate hikes in December and January. According to Timiraos, this could be one way to adjust the policy pace. The last time the Fed raised rates by more than 25 basis points at once was back in 2022. On social media, Timiraos further broke down the details of core inflation, pointing out that core prices “strengthened broadly” in October. Specifically, core goods prices rose at a 1% annualized pace over the past six months, compared with just 0.1% in the previous period through June; core services prices excluding shelter rose 0.4% in October, about 4.9% annualized, while three- and six-month annualized increases stood at 5.5% and 3.2% respectively. He also pointed out that the unrounded month-on-month increase in core CPI for October was 0.296%, marking the third straight month at about 0.3%. The three-month annualized rate for core CPI climbed to 3.75%, compared with only 1.6% in July. This data shows that inflationary pressures are not just driven by overall energy price increases—core goods and services prices are also consistently strengthening. For the Fed, this makes it harder to treat inflation as a short-term shock and simply wait for price pressures to subside on their own. Waller raises 50-basis-point option, market begins to reassess policy strength Just hours before the CPI was released, Waller gave a hawkish speech while attending an event in London. He said the US economy was experiencing strong growth and a stable labor market, but inflation remained too high, requiring the Fed to “tighten policy sooner rather than later.” Waller had previously supported the Fed’s decision to keep rates unchanged at the last meeting, arguing that previous policy communications had already led financial markets to price in some degree of tightening. He believes policy adjustments do not have to be implemented in consecutive meetings, but prior guidance on rate hikes must eventually be delivered on, otherwise markets may lower expectations for further tightening, causing financial conditions to ease prematurely. Regarding the December meeting, Waller had already indicated before the CPI was published that if the October core CPI once again rose by around 0.3% month-on-month (as in the previous two months) or even higher, more forceful policy action might be needed. He explicitly raised the possibility of a 50-basis-point hike, and warned that if inflation remained high and price pressures broadened, raising rates by only 25 basis points could hurt the Fed’s credibility in fighting inflation. Ultimately, the October core CPI met this threshold. According to Reuters, after the data was announced, market expectations for a 25-basis-point rate hike in December were almost certain, and bets on a 50-basis-point hike rose to about 15% at one point. The two-year US Treasury yield surged, recording its largest single-day rise since early April 2025. However, Timiraos also cautioned that no other Fed official has publicly echoed Waller’s 50-basis-point position so far. Thus, the market’s discussion of a larger rate hike does not necessarily mean consensus within the Fed. Wall Street divided: Inflation pressures cannot be ignored, but 50 basis points is not a consensus After the inflation data was released, several Wall Street figures said the reasons for a December Fed rate hike had increased, but assessments of the scale and the persistence of inflation pressures varied. Omair Sharif, President of Inflation Insights, commented that the latest report “offers little to ease market concerns about persistent inflation risks” and does not dispel the Fed’s reasons for further hikes. He also estimated that the October core PCE price index might climb by 0.34%, representing an annualized increase of over 4%, higher than the previous month. While the Fed’s 2% policy target is based on headline PCE inflation, core PCE better reflects the underlying inflation trend. If this estimate is confirmed by subsequent data, it would further justify Fed tightening. James McCann, Senior Economist at Edward Jones, described this as another “disappointing inflation report,” reflecting that underlying price pressures may be building again. With US economic growth and the labor market both clearly accelerating this year, and core inflation showing signs of reacceleration, the Fed faces even greater policy pressure. McCann pointed out that the real worry is whether inflation is settling at a higher level. He argued the report at least solidifies the rationale for a 25-basis-point hike in December, while the bigger debate has become whether the Fed needs a 50-basis-point hike and more aggressive action. Peter Cardillo, Chief Market Economist at Spartan Capital Securities, also believes a December rate hike is virtually certain, with the suspense lying in whether it will be 25 or 50 basis points. He commented that Waller has effectively paved the way for a half-point hike, and the latest data shows inflation remains an issue. However, Cardillo also cautioned that circumstances could still change over the next 30 to 40 days. Should oil prices retreat and pass through to consumer prices, inflationary pressures may ease; but if oil rebounds, the inflation outlook could deteriorate again. Chris Zaccarelli, Chief Investment Officer at Northlight Asset Management, believes inflation above an ideal level further increases the likelihood of a December Fed hike. Still, despite market calls for a 50-basis-point hike, he expects the Fed will only lift rates by 25 basis points next month. Joe Saluzzi, Co-Head of Themis Trading, likewise noted that persistently high core inflation shows that price pressures have “stickiness” and that a 25-basis-point hike remains realistic, while 50 basis points may be too aggressive. He also warned that prolonged high rates and inflation will continue to pressure borrowing-dependent businesses, affecting profits and stock valuations. Skyler Weinand, Chief Investment Officer at Regan Capital, stated that the latest CPI paves the way for another Fed rate hike in December—the central bank cannot ignore the clear rebound in inflation data. He also pointed out that the latest jobs report showed robust employment gains in October as well as upward revisions to previous months’ data, providing the Fed with more room for further hikes. Labor market remains resilient, tightening policies may persist longer Besides inflation itself, the continued resilience of the US labor market also provides the Fed more leeway to prioritize combating inflation in its policy decisions. In his speech on Tuesday, Waller noted that US unemployment fell to 4.1% in October, with 165,000 new jobs added that month and a combined upward revision of 85,000 jobs over the prior two months. Although the average monthly jobs gains over the past six and twelve months is about 80,000, the overall labor market remains in a broadly balanced state, with no significant deterioration. This means the Fed, faced with persistently high inflation, need not worry about the impact of rate hikes on jobs as much as it would if the labor market were visibly weakening. Brian Jacobsen, Chief Economic Strategist at Annex Wealth Management, pointed out from a price transmission angle that three consecutive months of core CPI rising 0.3% month-on-month shows that the issue isn’t just high headline CPI, but that energy shocks may have begun to seep into core inflation. He also mentioned that Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee previously discussed how AI demand could be a new source of inflationary pressure for the Fed. As AI investment and infrastructure expansion rise, economic activity may crowd out resources in other areas and push up prices for some services. Jacobsen suggests the Fed may increasingly focus on the resource squeeze from AI demand and rising wage costs for skilled trades like plumbers and electricians. Jeff Schulze, Chief Investment Strategist at Franklin Templeton Institute, warned that the latest inflation data will serve as a headwind for risk assets. Investors are beginning to price in a 50-basis-point December hike and more afterward; rising short-term yields and a stronger US dollar could both suppress equity valuations. Karen Manna, Fixed Income Investment Strategist at Federated Hermes, also said the report strengthens the rationale for another Fed rate hike and further demands policymakers maintain vigilance. The real concern for investors is that if inflation remains high, the Fed may have to keep monetary policy restrictive for an extended period, well into 2027. Overall, the October CPI brings a December rate hike closer to market consensus, but the policy options facing the Fed are no longer just whether to raise rates. Waller’s 50-basis-point option, Timiraos’ comments on rate-hike spacing, and whether other officials will support speeding up the pace of tightening—all will be key market focuses going forward.

items.title: CPI Deals a Blow to US Bonds! 2-Year Yield Surges Over 20 Basis Points Intraday, Gold and Silver Plunge
items.author: 华尔街见闻
items.creator: 华尔街见闻
items.summary: After the release of the CPI, traders began to expect a lower likelihood of a 50 basis point rate hike in December; this year’s Federal Reserve voting member Logan stated that a faster pace of rate hikes may be needed this winter, with at least two more 25 basis point hikes required before pausing. Subsequently, the rise in U.S. Treasury yields continued to widen, with the 10-year yield climbing back above 5.0% and rising more than 10 basis points intraday; spot gold once fell over 3%, while spot silver at one point dropped more than 4%.
items.body: In October, U.S. inflation once again exceeded market expectations, triggering a sell-off in U.S. Treasury bonds and a sharp rise in yields across the board. The strengthening U.S. dollar and heightened expectations for higher interest rates also put pressure on gold and silver. With Federal Reserve officials repeatedly sending hawkish signals, markets are not only increasingly betting on a rate hike in December but are also beginning to assess the possibility of a larger hike and further monetary policy tightening into next year. On Tuesday, U.S. Eastern Time, after the release of the U.S. CPI data, U.S. Treasuries were heavily sold, sending prices plunging and yields accelerating higher. The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield expanded its gains following the CPI release and, after remarks by Federal Reserve official Lorie Logan, briefly broke above 5.01% during the U.S. stock market midday session, rising more than 10 basis points on the day. The 2-year Treasury yield, which is more sensitive to Fed policy expectations, climbed even more, surpassing 4.77% during midday and jumping more than 20 basis points on the day, on course for its biggest single-day surge since April last year. Precious metals markets also came under pressure. After the U.S. CPI release, gold extended its losses during the session. In the U.S. stock market midday, New York gold futures hit an intraday low of $4,020.8 per ounce, dropping nearly 2.3% on the day; spot gold fell below $4,014 per ounce, down nearly 3.1% intraday. The decline in silver was even more pronounced. Market data shows that at the day's lows in New York's midday, silver futures fell nearly 3% intraday, while spot silver plunged over 4%. CPI Inflation Continues to Beat Expectations for Months, Bond Market Reprices Fed Policy Path The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Tuesday that October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month, higher than the market expectation of 0.3%, but slowed from 0.6% in September. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy prices, also rose 0.3% month-on-month, surpassing expectations of 0.2% and matching September’s increase. This marks the third consecutive month of 0.3% gains for core CPI. Due to the U.S. federal government shutdown at the same time last year, which prevented data collection, the Bureau did not release year-on-year CPI data for October. Just hours before the CPI data was released, the market was already rattled by hawkish remarks from Fed Governor Christopher Waller. In a speech in London on Tuesday, Waller said that even if inflation improved in October, he would still be inclined to support a 25 basis point Fed rate hike in December. However, if core CPI reached 0.3% or higher for a third straight month, the Fed should consider a 50 basis point hike in December. He warned that raising rates by only 25 basis points could undermine the credibility of the Fed’s fight against inflation. The actual core CPI published hit Waller’s 0.3% threshold precisely. After the data release, markets quickly ramped up bets on a larger rate hike. Reuters reported that traders’ implied probability of a 50 basis point hike by the Fed in December spiked to about 13.6%, from near zero before the data was released; by contrast, a 25 basis point hike had already become the mainstream market expectation. According to Bloomberg, the inflation data triggered a sell-off in Treasuries, with short-term maturities bearing the brunt. Money markets also increased bets that the Fed will hike rates at least two more times by mid-2027, and began more clearly pricing in the possibility of a one-off 50 basis point hike in December. Lindsay Rosner, Head of Multi-Sector Fixed Income Investing at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, said that if CPI remains robust, the Fed may usher in a more aggressive tightening cycle. Her view reflects market worries over persistently high inflation: even if a December hike is now the baseline expectation, future policy rates could still be more hawkish than previously anticipated. This Year’s FOMC Voter Logan: Faster Rate Hikes May Be Needed This Winter, Fed Needs at Least Two More 25 Basis Point Hikes Before a Pause Following the CPI release, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan also sent further signals of policy tightening. Logan is a voting member of the FOMC this year. Speaking at an energy conference co-hosted by the Dallas Fed and the Kansas City Fed on Tuesday, she said that given current economic and inflation prospects, the Fed still needs to implement at least two additional 25 basis point hikes. Logan noted that the specific pace of hikes depends on the near-term economic and financial environment, and that the Fed might need to move faster this winter than it has this autumn. She stated, "It may be necessary this winter to act more quickly than the FOMC has so far this autumn." However, Logan is not advocating for continuous rate hikes. She said that after completing these two hikes, the Fed could pause to assess the economy and financial markets before deciding on further policy adjustments. She also emphasized that if inflation remains above target for an extended period, it could gradually become entrenched in business and household expectations, making timely action crucial. Logan’s comments signal that some Fed officials are discussing not just whether to hike rates in December, but also how to reach a moderately restrictive level more quickly. Her statements echoed Waller’s, further fueling market concerns about the Fed tightening policy even more over the coming months. U.S. Treasury Yields and Dollar Rise Together, Doubling Pressure on Gold and Silver Both U.S. Treasury yields and the dollar are strengthening, putting pressure on non-yielding precious metals. On one hand, higher bond yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets like gold and silver; on the other hand, a stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated precious metals more expensive for holders of other currencies. According to Reuters, after October inflation data came in higher than expected, gold prices fell noticeably as the market began evaluating the chances of the Fed taking a more aggressive rate-hiking stance. Gold is especially sensitive to changes in interest rate expectations, and if the market further raises its outlook for policy rates, precious metals could continue to face pressure in the short term. However, the future path for gold and silver will not depend solely on Fed policy. Movements in the dollar, geopolitical risks, energy prices, and investors’ outlook on the economy can all affect demand for precious metals. The key market shift currently is that both the inflation data and hawkish comments from Fed officials have reinforced expectations for higher rates, forcing a reset in precious metals trades that previously benefited from rate-cut expectations.

Subsequently, the rise in U.S. Treasury yields continued to widen, with the 10-year yield climbing back above 5.0% and rising more than 10 basis points intraday; spot gold once fell over 3%, while spot silver at one point dropped more than 4%.

MADRID, Nov 10 : Spain's government has demanded that TikTok suspend its operations in Spain until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, after a media report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views.
Youth Minister Sira Rego, whose ministry cannot singlehandedly ban the platform in Spain, has appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company, according to a statement by the ministry.
"Social media cannot be lawless territory," Rego said.
The request comes months after Sanchez's government requested a probe into X, Meta and TikTok for allegedly spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material, as European regulators intensify scrutiny of big tech over harmful and illegal content.

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 10 : US electricity consumption will rise to record highs in 2026 and 2027 due to power-hungry AI data centers and electrification, the US Energy Information Administration said in its Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) on Tuesday.
The EIA projected that power demand will rise from a record 4,216 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) in 2025 to 4,306 billion kWh in 2026 and 4,370 billion kWh in 2027. If correct, 2026 would be the third year in a row of record demand.
Demand is surging largely due to data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. Homes and businesses have also been relying more on electricity and less on fossil fuels for heat and transportation.
The EIA forecast that power sales in 2026 will rise to 1,546 billion kWh for residential consumers, 1,557 billion kWh for commercial customers and 1,061 billion kWh for industrial customers.

The all-time highs stand at 1,519 billion kWh for residential consumers and 1,503 billion kWh for commercial customers in 2025 and 1,064 billion kWh for industrial customers in 2000.
As renewable output rises, the EIA said the share of power generation from coal will slide from 17 per cent in 2025 to 15 per cent in 2026 and 2027, while the share of natural gas in 2026 will hold steady from 2025 at 40 per cent, then ease to 39 per cent in 2027.
The percentage of renewable generation will rise from around 24 per cent in 2025 to 25 per cent in 2026 and 28 per cent in 2027, while nuclear power's share will hold at 18 per cent in 2026 and 2027, the same as in 2025, according to the outlook.
The EIA projected that gas sales in 2026 would slide to 12.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) for residential consumers and 9.4 bcfd for commercial customers, but rise to 23.8 bcfd for industrial customers and 37.4 bcfd for power generation.
Those figures compare with all-time highs of 14.3 bcfd in 1996 for residential consumers, 9.9 bcfd in 2025 for commercial customers, 23.8 bcfd in 1973 for industrial customers, and 36.8 bcfd in 2024 for power generation.

Goldman Sachs, Citi Back $270M Stablecoin Venture to Challenge Tether, Circle Less than 1 min read

GS C USDTUSD CRCL
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. GS , Citigroup Inc. C and other major financial institutions have reportedly committed $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture targeting a launch in the first half of 2027.
The initiative, known as Project Faro , aims to challenge the dominance of Tether USDTUSD and Circle Internet Group Inc. CRCL in the roughly $290 billion stablecoin market.
Bloomberg reported Tuesday the funding will cover five years of operations for a new U.S.-based stablecoin issuer.
The venture includes 21 financial institutions, with Banco Santander, Deutsche Bank, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments, UBS and Lloyds Banking Group among its participants.
The initiative follows growing interest among traditional banks in blockchain-based payments, particularly after the U.S. passed stablecoin legislation in 2025.
Can Wall Street Challenge Tether And Circle?
Tether and Circle Internet Group Inc. currently control almost 85% of the global stablecoin market. Their dominance presents a major challenge for new entrants despite growing institutional interest.
Visa, Mastercard and Stripe are among more than 100 companies backing stablecoin issuer Open Standard, while European banks have established Qivalis to develop a euro-denominated stablecoin.
Project Faro’s biggest advantage could be its participating banks’ existing customer networks and payment infrastructure. Disclaimer Preview Image: Shutterstock

Nov 10 : OpenAI said on Tuesday it was launching "Businesses" in beta within ChatGPT, giving companies a way to claim and manage their profiles, update information and track how users engage with them on the chatbot.
• Through a tool called "Business Hub", companies can claim their business in ChatGPT and, once verified, update key details and add product feeds with pricing and availability

• Another tool called "Business Agents" will let people chat with an agent from a business to ask about its products or services. OpenAI is initially rolling out the feature to eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the US

NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China 1 min read

NVDA
NVIDIA NVDA shares fell 4.43% to $170.75 as of 9:53 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 10, after The Information reported that Jensen Huang's personal relationship with a businesswoman alleged to work for Beijing helped move at least $7.5 billion of its chips to Chinese firms. That stacks on Monday's 4.27% drop. Reuters, which carried the report, said it could not independently verify the claims.
The report describes a web of companies in China and Singapore, centered on Shanghai Century Litong, that won preferred cloud-partner status within months of its June 2023 founding. When orders for export-restricted chips stalled, roughly 240,000 H100, H200 and A100 units allegedly reached China. Some of that capacity reportedly served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs. The company's board said a committee of independent directors with outside counsel is running the review. The board added that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

From the November 6 close of $186.64, the two-day slide is 8.51%, roughly $383 billion of market value on about 24.1 billion shares. The GuruFocus profile is lopsided: GF Score 92/100, Profitability 10/10, Financial Strength 9/10 and Momentum 10/10, but GF Value Rank only 2/10. At $170.75 the shares trade 60.10% below the $427.93 GF Value, yet GuruFocus itself tags the setup "Possible Value Trap, Think Twice." The model gap alone is no bargain signal. The next hard test is the November 17 third-quarter report, where any export-control questions would surface in guidance or disclosures.

items.title: Bolsa Mexicana espera nuevas emisiones de acciones en 2027: qué falta para atraer capital
items.author: Carlos Rodríguez Salcedo
items.summary: Representantes de BlackRock, Vanguard, la BMV y Bitso analizaron los desafíos de liquidez, regulación y acceso a la inversión durante el Bloomberg Línea Summit México 2026.
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — La Bolsa Mexicana de Valores (BMV) espera concretar emisiones simplificadas de acciones en 2027, una de las oportunidades para impulsar el mercado de capitales mexicano, cuyos retos de liquidez, regulación y acceso a la inversión marcaron el debate durante el Bloomberg Línea Summit México 2026 . Ver más: Cinco razones por las que Wall Street puede seguir subiendo en los últimos meses de 2026 El objetivo forma parte de los esfuerzos de la industria financiera para ampliar el acceso al mercado de capitales, atraer nuevas empresas y superar los obstáculos de liquidez, regulación y participación de inversionistas. El panel reunió a Sergio Méndez, de BlackRock México ( BLK ); Juan Hernández, de Vanguard; Jorge Alegría, de la BMV, y Felipe Vallejo, de Bitso México. “Estamos esperando que sí”, respondió Alegría al ser consultado sobre la posibilidad de concretar emisiones simplificadas de acciones en 2027, después de que la bolsa completara su primera operación de deuda bajo este mecanismo. La financiera no bancaria Adventus Capital realizó el 7 de octubre la primera emisión simplificada de deuda de la BMV, por MXN$560 millones (US$31 millones). La operación se completó en cinco semanas, frente a los seis meses que habría requerido un proceso tradicional. La BMV tiene en marcha un proceso confidencial de listado de una empresa que busca emitir acciones bajo el esquema simplificado. Este mecanismo agiliza las colocaciones y está reservado a inversionistas institucionales y calificados. La diferencia entre ambos segmentos es significativa. Mientras el mercado de deuda mexicano acumulaba más de MXN$580.000 millones en financiamiento durante 2026, las nuevas colocaciones accionarias continuaban limitadas. Suscríbete al newsletter Línea de Mercado , una selección de Bloomberg Línea con las noticias bursátiles más destacadas del día. Alegría sostuvo que “tenemos que aumentar mucho más la liquidez de las acciones que ya existen”, una condición que considera necesaria para fortalecer la confianza de los inversionistas mexicanos. El crecimiento de la demanda también depende de los incentivos para canalizar recursos hacia instrumentos de largo plazo, según Sergio Méndez, de BlackRock México, quien planteó revisar aspectos fiscales y regulatorios. Méndez destacó el préstamo de valores como una herramienta que puede contribuir a incrementar la liquidez y mejorar las condiciones de operación del mercado. La industria de fondos ofrece otra perspectiva sobre la evolución del ahorro financiero. Juan Hernández, de Vanguard, destacó que estos vehículos administran MXN$5,3 billones y acumulan aproximadamente 20 millones de cuentas. Hace 15 años, la exposición a renta variable y fondos multiactivos representaba apenas el 2% de la industria. Actualmente, la participación de estos instrumentos supera el 25%, según las cifras presentadas por Hernández. El Sistema Internacional de Cotizaciones (SIC) también ha ampliado las alternativas disponibles, con más de 4.000 valores, entre ellos cerca de 2.000 fondos cotizados en bolsa (ETF). Ver más: Exclusiva: CFE evalúa emisión por US$2.000 millones para Fibra con activos de generación eléctrica Sin embargo, el acceso a instrumentos internacionales contrasta con la necesidad de fortalecer la negociación de acciones mexicanas, particularmente entre inversionistas que ya participan en compañías extranjeras. La BMV busca que empresas como Bimbo ( BIMBOA ), FEMSA ( FEMSAUBD ), Televisa ( TLEVICPO ) y América Móvil ( AMXB ) despierten un interés comparable al que generan Tesla ( TSLA ), Amazon ( AMZN ) y otras compañías internacionales. La expansión de las plataformas digitales ha facilitado la apertura de cuentas bursátiles, pero el crecimiento del acceso no necesariamente se ha traducido en una mayor participación en acciones. Felipe Vallejo, de Bitso México, explicó que una encuesta entre clientes con activos en la plataforma encontró que solamente el 10% había invertido en bolsa, ya fuera mexicana o internacional. Para la compañía, la oportunidad consiste en facilitar la distribución de productos financieros y reducir las barreras que todavía separan a los usuarios digitales de los mercados bursátiles. “Creo que solo falta hacerlo bien, bien fácil”, afirmó Vallejo al referirse a la experiencia que necesitan los inversionistas minoristas. Ver más: Emisión simplificada en Bolsa Mexicana despertó interés para más listados en deuda y acciones: CEO La disponibilidad de servicios fuera del horario bancario es otro factor. Según Bitso, un tercio del volumen de su servicio de inversión Invierto se registra cuando las instituciones financieras tradicionales no están abiertas. La compañía considera que los horarios extendidos responden a los hábitos de personas que revisan sus inversiones después de concluir su jornada laboral. La BMV también contempla ampliar sus horarios de negociación. Actualmente, determinados productos derivados ya operan durante sesiones extendidas, mientras la infraestructura tecnológica se prepara para nuevas modalidades. No obstante, la ampliación exige coordinación entre bancos, intermediarios, sistemas de liquidación y autoridades, además de la capacidad tecnológica de las plataformas. La bolsa desarrolla una modernización de sus sistemas de negociación, custodia y posnegociación, con tecnología de Nasdaq y cambios en la infraestructura de Indeval. La primera etapa está prevista para 2027 y la última para 2028. El proyecto también busca integrar información que actualmente se encuentra distribuida entre diferentes plataformas y entidades del mercado. Ver más: Financiera Adventus Capital realiza la primera emisión simplificada de deuda en la Bolsa Mexicana La disponibilidad de datos permitiría desarrollar herramientas para analistas, inversionistas y sistemas de inteligencia artificial, además de mejorar los procesos de información y supervisión. El acceso tecnológico, sin embargo, representa solamente una parte del desafío. Vanguard identificó la asesoría financiera como uno de los principales espacios pendientes de desarrollo. Hernández estimó que México cuenta con entre 9.000 y 10.000 asesores de inversión para una población cercana a 130 millones de habitantes, una proporción reducida frente a otros mercados. Como referencia, señaló que Brasil pasó de aproximadamente 5.000 a 30.000 asesores durante los últimos seis años, mientras Estados Unidos dispone de unos 300.000 profesionales. La digitalización podría reducir el costo de la asesoría y facilitar el acceso a servicios que tradicionalmente requieren patrimonios elevados. Aun así, Vanguard considera que las herramientas automatizadas no sustituyen por completo la relación con un asesor, especialmente cuando las personas deben tomar decisiones patrimoniales relevantes. Ver más: Bonos de Venezuela enfrentan riesgo de más pérdidas: la alerta de una consultora de EE.UU. Méndez, de BlackRock, insistió en que la educación financiera debe acompañar la expansión de las plataformas, particularmente para evitar decisiones motivadas por movimientos de corto plazo. “Invertir es un proceso de generación de rendimientos de largo plazo”, sostuvo durante su intervención. La diversificación también ocupó un lugar central en la discusión. Vanguard destacó que la asignación entre acciones, bonos, divisas y otros instrumentos explica una proporción importante del comportamiento de los portafolios. Hernández resumió los principios de inversión de la administradora en planificación, diversificación, control de costos y disciplina para mantener una estrategia durante episodios de volatilidad. La transformación del mercado mexicano también estará condicionada por tendencias internacionales, entre ellas la inteligencia artificial, la fragmentación geopolítica y los cambios demográficos. BlackRock identificó oportunidades relacionadas con infraestructura tecnológica, centros de datos, semiconductores y necesidades de financiamiento para sostener la expansión de nuevas capacidades productivas. Ver más: Goldman Sachs recorta su previsión para el precio del oro: ¿cuál es su proyección para 2027? Méndez consideró que “la necesidad de capital en el mundo para financiar este cambio económico es otra realidad”, en referencia a la magnitud de las inversiones requeridas por las grandes compañías tecnológicas. La reorganización de las cadenas de suministro y la consolidación de bloques económicos también forman parte de las tendencias identificadas por la administradora. En particular, BlackRock destacó las oportunidades asociadas con Norteamérica, aunque reconoció que las tensiones políticas pueden introducir incertidumbre en las decisiones de inversión. Vanguard comparó la expansión de la inteligencia artificial con transformaciones históricas de infraestructura, por la magnitud del gasto de capital destinado a centros de datos y capacidad tecnológica. Hernández planteó un escenario de crecimiento de Estados Unidos cercano al 3%, impulsado por la inversión tecnológica, aunque advirtió sobre la importancia de que ese gasto se traduzca en productividad. La discusión también abordó el envejecimiento de la población y la disminución de las tasas de fecundidad, factores que podrían modificar las necesidades de inversión y las perspectivas económicas. Ver más: Una guía para invertir tras resultados de elecciones en EE.UU.: acciones, bonos, dólar y oro Desde Bitso, Vallejo destacó la relación entre los cambios demográficos y la inteligencia artificial, particularmente por sus posibles efectos sobre la productividad. En el terreno financiero, la compañía distinguió entre el desarrollo de las stablecoins y los mercados de predicción, dos segmentos que atraviesan etapas regulatorias diferentes. Las monedas estables ya tienen aplicaciones en pagos internacionales y remesas. En México, Bitso destacó su utilización para transferencias transfronterizas, mientras en Argentina identificó una demanda vinculada al resguardo de valor. “Ya el mundo está regulando esto y ya lo está usando”, afirmó Vallejo al referirse al avance internacional de las stablecoins . Los mercados de predicción, por su parte, mantienen interrogantes regulatorios, especialmente sobre su clasificación como instrumentos financieros o mecanismos de apuestas. Aunque Bitso identificó posibles aplicaciones para cobertura de riesgos, consideró necesario evaluar su funcionamiento y sus efectos antes de impulsar una regulación específica en México. Ver más: Soja, trigo y fertilizantes: Banco Mundial prevé más presión sobre el precio de los alimentos La tokenización también apareció entre las alternativas futuras del mercado, aunque tanto la BMV como Bitso coincidieron en priorizar la infraestructura, la liquidez y la digitalización. En materia regulatoria, la bolsa identificó el préstamo de valores, las operaciones de reporto y la liquidación de derivados como prioridades para mejorar el funcionamiento del mercado. Alegría sostuvo que estos cambios podrían tener efectos importantes sobre la negociación bursátil, incluso sin necesidad de reformas estructurales de mayor alcance. Para Bitso, otra oportunidad consiste en orientar parte de la inclusión financiera hacia productos de inversión y financiamiento para empresas, en lugar de concentrarla en el crédito al consumo. El avance de estas iniciativas dependerá de las autorizaciones regulatorias, la adopción tecnológica y la respuesta de los inversionistas, mientras la BMV prepara sus siguientes etapas de modernización y nuevas colocaciones para 2027.

items.title: エヌビディア時価総額、2日間で4300億ドル消失　ＣＥＯ不倫騒動で
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Aishwarya Venugopal　David Shepardson　Courtney Rozen

[１０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Aishwarya Venugopal　David Shepardson　Courtney Rozen

[１０日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手エヌビディアの時価総額が２営業日で約４３００億ドル消失した。同社のジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）と、スパイとされる中国人女性との不倫騒動の影響が広がっている。

同社株は、不倫に関する報道が出る前は年初来ほぼ横ばいで推移していたが、報道以来９．５％下落した。

１０日には、フアン氏と中国人女性との関係が少なくとも７５億ドル相当の同社製半導体の中国向け出荷を後押ししたとの疑惑や、ルビオ国務長官がこの不倫関係についてトランプ大統領に以前報告していたとの報道が浮上し、問題が多方面に広がった。上院民主党トップのシューマー院内総務は政権による説明と、対中半導体輸出規制の強化を要求。エヌビディアの独立取締役は調査のため外部弁護士を起用した。

フアン氏個人を巡る問題は、エヌビディア全体のリスクに発展している。フアン氏は３０年以上にわたってエヌビディアを率い、同社を人工知能（ＡＩ）向け半導体の圧倒的な供給企業に育てた。一連の疑惑を受けて、同社の企業統治のあり方や、フアン氏への過度な依存を懸念する声が上がっている。

米連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）は、フアン氏が外国の情報活動の標的となっていたかどうかを調べている。フアン氏は従業員に対し、妻に対して不貞行為を働いたことを認めたが、関係の詳細は明らかにしていない。

米ＣＮＢＣによると、フアン氏は９日の非公開会合で、事業に関する議論に入る前に経営幹部に謝罪。１０日にはエヌビディア本社で再び会議を開いたという。

エヌビディアによると、取締役会は米国の国家安全保障や同社の機密が損なわれたと考える理由はないとしており、フアン氏は社内調査への協力を約束している。取締役会は調査を主導する弁護士として、法律事務所ワクテル・リプトンのパートナーで、ニューヨーク南部地区の連邦検事代行を務めたジュン・キム氏を起用した。

米紙ニューヨーク・タイムズは１０日、ルビオ氏が中国に向かう大統領専用機エアフォース・ワンの機内で、中国のスパイと見られる女性とフアン氏が関係を持っていたとの米情報機関の情報をトランプ氏に報告していたと報じた。同紙が事情を知る関係者の話として伝えたところによると、トランプ氏がこの情報に関する報告を受けたのは、７カ月間で少なくとも２回目だった。

トランプ氏は９日、フアン氏と話をしたとした上で、フアン氏からその女性がスパイであるとは全く知らなかったと伝えられたと説明。「私は彼に『彼女がスパイだとは知っていたのか？』と尋ねた。彼は『彼女がスパイだとは全く知らなかった』と答え、私は彼を心から信じている」と語った。

トランプ氏はまた、５月の訪中にフアン氏が同行した際には、疑惑の関係について知らなかったと述べた。

items.title: Defiant Hegseth blasts impeachment effort ahead of House vote
items.author: CNA
items.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth also thanked US President Donald Trump for his support as lawmakers prepared to vote on eight articles of impeachment against him.

Defiant Hegseth blasts impeachment effort ahead of House vote

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth also thanked US President Donald Trump for his support as lawmakers prepared to vote on eight articles of impeachment against him.

US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth holds a press briefing at the Pentagon in Washington, DC, on Nov 10, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein)

11 Nov 2026 01:32AM
(Updated: 11 Nov 2026 06:54AM)

WASHINGTON: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday (Nov 10) blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce that would embolden US adversaries, as he lashed out at his political opponents in Congress and the media in an unapologetic defence of his record.
Striking a defiant tone at a Pentagon news briefing, Hegseth thanked US President Donald Trump for his continued support as the House of Representatives scheduled a procedural vote for late Tuesday that will test support for his impeachment.
Hegseth said past impeachments of Trump had ultimately failed, and added: "Both times he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now they're trying a third time. This time against a member of his cabinet."
US Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced eight articles of impeachment against H egseth on Monday. Massie said in a post on X that if the House of Representatives can overcome Tuesday's procedural effort, "we will proceed to a real debate and vote on the Articles of Impeachment".

Congressional sources say the resolution may have the votes to pass even with Trump’s Republicans still controlling the House until Democrats take over on Jan 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds majority is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats.
Hegseth is accused of various abuses of power in office, including issuing orders to go to war with Iran without an imminent threat or approval from Congress.
Voter anger over the Iran war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week's midterm elections . A new Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday found a majority of Americans want the newly elected Democratic-majority US Congress to act to end the war with Iran.

US Representative Thomas Massie holds a press conference about his resolution to impeach Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth, on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC, on Nov 9, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein)

Vice President JD Vance has publicly questioned the war. Hegseth declined to be drawn into responding to Vance, but defended the conflict, calling Trump courageous and saying Iran's military has been left in ruins.
"History will judge the Iran war quite differently than the conventional wisdom right now," he said.
Hegseth cited US Secretary of State Marco Rubio as saying of the war: "It's not necessarily popular, but it may have been necessary, and that's certainly how I feel. It was a necessary undertaking."
Trump repeated his backing of Hegseth in a post on his Truth Social platform just after the Pentagon briefing ended.
"Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!" he wrote.
A polarising figure in American politics, Hegseth would be the first US defense secretary to be impeached. The last time any civilian leader of the US military was impeached was in 1876, when William Belknap held the title "secretary of war".
Hegseth, a former Fox News host, calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and "woke" when he took office last year.
But even some Republicans say his strained relations with Congress are becoming a political liability as the administration seeks a US$1.5 trillion defense spending package.
In a possible nod to the spending requests, Hegseth said Republicans should use their final weeks in control of Congress to deliver wins for the American people instead of pursuing his impeachment.
If he's still around next year, Democrats have promised to investigate Hegseth and his handling of the Pentagon, including his firing of the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and other top military officers.

Nov 10 : Anthropic said on Tuesday it was bringing its Claude assistant to video conference platform Google Meet, as the company pushes to integrate AI deeper into everyday office work.
Earlier in the day, Anthropic launched a roadshow for its highly anticipated US initial public offering, with plans to raise as much as $64.4 billion at a $1.02 trillion valuation. The offering will test investors' appetite for the AI boom and Anthropic's massive spending plans.
Called Claude Meetings, the new feature will let users add Claude to video calls as a visible participant. Anthropic said Claude would be able to follow the conversation and turn discussions into work in real time, while also drafting plans, creating timelines and answering questions in the call's chat.
The feature is designed to shift AI's role in meetings from simply recording or summarizing conversations to doing the work that follows from them while the discussion is still taking place, Anthropic said.

Nov 10 : IBM said on Tuesday that it was ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people.
The move comes amid tight scrutiny of foreign tech hiring by Donald Trump's administration. Last month, it suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several major outsourcers, including Cognizant, Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services, from the Permanent Labor Certification process — a key step toward green cards for foreign workers.
IBM Consulting has used US high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages, but participation has been declining for years, a company spokesperson told Reuters.
It opted to end sponsorship for most such roles as skill availability and client needs have evolved, the spokesperson added.
